maria-cs: morning — putting together the go-live plan for DeltaCorp's Dedicated pool. need a short checklist for quota + autoscale + smoke load tests. can we sync on times? :wave:
vikram-ops: I can own quota numbers. current commitment: 120k reqs/day, peak burst target 1.5k rps. thinking reserved pool of 4 GPUs with autoscale up to 8 for bursts.
lee-sre: for load tests i'd like a 3-stage: soak (30m @ 60% peak), ramp (15m to 100% peak), spike (5m @ 150% peak). target window 02:00-04:00 UTC to avoid customer traffic.
tara-ml: model notes — kv-cache cold start ~20s on first big prompt, recommend warmup script priming common prefixes. also suggest small-quant models for fallback.
maria-cs: timeline idea: Thurs 03:00 UTC smoke, Fri 02:00 full soak + spike. delta ok with Thurs smoke. olivia-customer: confirmed Thurs smoke ok for us, Fri is fine but please keep it to 02-05 UTC.
vikram-ops: quota plan draft:
- reserved pool: 4x A100-sim nodes (logical)
- min_instances: 4
- autoscale: cpu/queue based + token-rate trigger
- max_instances: 8
- warmup concurrency: 8 threads per node
- circuit-breaker: failover to smaller model at >80% queue
lee-sre: autoscale math check: with batch size 8 and avg latency 120ms, one instance ~ (1 / 0.12) * 8 = ~67 rps effective. 4 instances ~268 rps. need ~1.5k rps -> we need different packing or more nodes.
tara-ml: right — we should use continuous batching and prefix caching. with continuous batching optimizations we observed >200 rps per A100 for seq len 64. i'll attach perf numbers after lunch.
maria-cs: action items so far: vikram finalize quota json, lee create loadscript, tara provide perf numbers + warmup snippets, i'll coordinate with Delta on exact window and runbook.
lee-sre: loadscript (locust) quick snippet:
```
from locust import HttpUser, task, between
class DeltaUser(HttpUser):
  wait_time = between(0.01, 0.05)
  @task
  def infer(self):
    self.client.post('/v1/generate', json={"prompt": "summarize: ..."})
```
run: `LOCUST_USERS=1500 locust -f locustfile.py --headless --run-time 00:50:00`
vikram-ops: i'll post the quota PR to infra repo after lunch: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/642 (wip). will include autoscale policy and failover map.
olivia-customer: quick ask — can you add a soft-rate-limit to protect our downstream billing spikes? we want a 95th percentile throttle before fallback kicks in.
tara-ml: agree, add a token-rate limiter at edge; also add a short-lived cache priming job that hits common user prefixes 5x per node. script example:
```
# warmup.sh
for i in {1..5}; do
  curl -sS -X POST $ENDPOINT -d '{"prompt":"Hello, summarize X"}' &
done
```
deploy-bot: scheduled warmup-job for 2024-11-07T02:30:00Z on cluster-delta (job id: warmup-171420).
maria-cs: perfect — please add rollback steps in runbook: how to scale down, how to switch to fallback model, contact matrix.
lee-sre: rollback checklist draft:
- abort load test (locust stop)
- set max_instances=4 on pool
- enable fallback route (model-small) via routing flag `fallback: true`
- monitor 5m p95 latency and errors
- if >5% errors, open INC and run DBR simulation
vikram-ops: i've added alerting knobs: queue_length > 200 -> pager to SRE, token_error_rate > 0.5% -> page oncall.
maria-cs: postmortem owner? tara or lee? want someone to own quality regression checks after full soak.
tara-ml: i'll own post-soak evals — will run promptset A/B and report BLEU/ROUGE delta + hallucination rate.
olivia-customer: thanks — can you also capture sample failing prompts so our engineering can triage?
tara-ml: yes, will capture top 50 failing prompts and push to shared drive.
maria-cs: last check: who will run the dry-run day before? lee?
lee-sre: i'll run Thurs smoke, olivia will verify. i'll post a short blameless runbook and the locust script into the thread.
maria-cs: OK team — i'll compile final runbook and send to Delta by EOD. tagging follow ups: @vikram-ops finalize PR, @tara-ml perf numbers + priming script, @lee-sre loadscript + runbook. :rocket:
vikram-ops: ack.
tara-ml: ack.
lee-sre: ack.
olivia-customer: thanks all, appreciate the clear plan. :raised_hands:
